title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 3: Local Government in Urban Areas

learn.hook: Who collects the garbage from millions of homes in Mumbai every morning? The city's own government!
points: Towns and cities have their own local governments called urban local bodies or municipal bodies.
Big cities have a municipal corporation, smaller cities and towns have a municipal council (nagar palika), and areas changing from village to town have a nagar panchayat.
A municipal corporation is led by an elected mayor. Its daily work is run by a municipal commissioner, an officer appointed by the state government.
Municipal bodies provide water supply, drainage, garbage collection, streetlights, roads, parks, public toilets and birth and death certificates.
They get money from taxes such as property tax, from fees, and from government grants. The 74th Amendment (1992) gave urban local bodies a place in the Constitution.

example.q: Delhi, a very large city, and a small hill town both need clean water. Which kind of municipal body would each most likely have?
steps: Very large cities have a municipal corporation.
Smaller towns have a municipal council (nagar palika).
Areas just turning from village to town have a nagar panchayat.
example.answer: The large city has a municipal corporation; the small town has a municipal council.

learn.reallife: When your family pays property tax or gets a birth certificate from the city office, they are dealing with the municipal body.

quiz.q: What kind of local body does a very large city usually have?
quiz.explain: Large cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and Chennai have municipal corporations.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rural and urban local bodies

quiz.q: Who is the elected head of a municipal corporation?
quiz.explain: The mayor is the elected head of a municipal corporation.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the head of a city with the head of a village

quiz.q: Who runs the day-to-day work of a municipal corporation?
quiz.explain: The municipal commissioner is an officer appointed by the state government to run daily work.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the elected mayor with the appointed commissioner

quiz.q: Which of these is a job of a municipal body?
quiz.explain: Municipal bodies keep cities clean and provide water, streetlights and more.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up local and national duties

quiz.q: What is a smaller city's or town's local body usually called?
quiz.explain: Smaller cities and towns have municipal councils.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every town has a corporation

quiz.q: Which amendment gave urban local bodies a place in the Constitution?
quiz.explain: The 74th Amendment (1992) is about urban local bodies; the 73rd is about panchayats.

quiz.q: Which tax is an important source of money for municipal bodies?
options: Income tax collected by the Union
quiz.explain: Owners of houses and buildings pay property tax to the municipal body.
quiz.mistake: Picks a tax collected by the Union government

quiz.q: An area is changing from a village into a town. What local body would it usually have?
quiz.explain: A nagar panchayat is set up for areas in transition from rural to urban.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about nagar panchayats

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Who keeps my city clean and lights up the streets at night?'
teach.praise: Thank you! Municipal bodies like the municipal corporation, led by a mayor, give us water, clean streets and streetlights!
teach.nudge: What is the city's local government called, and what services does it give us?

learn.hook: A big city is like a giant pizza cut into slices. Each slice is a ward with its own elected councillor!
points: A city is divided into smaller areas called wards.
The people of each ward elect a representative called a councillor (also called a corporator in big cities).
The councillor raises the ward's problems, like broken roads or water shortage, in the meetings of the municipal body.

In larger cities, nearby wards are grouped under ward committees, which deal with local problems closer to the people. The 74th Amendment provides for ward committees in cities with a population of three lakh or more.
Citizens play a role too: paying taxes, keeping streets clean, segregating wet and dry waste, and reporting problems to the councillor or ward office.

example.q: The drain in Arif's lane is blocked. What can his family do?
steps: The drain is a local, ward-level problem.
They can complain to the ward office or their elected councillor, or use the city's helpline or app.
The municipal body then sends workers to clear it.
example.answer: Report it to the ward office or the ward councillor.

learn.reallife: Many cities have helplines and apps where residents can post a photo of a pothole or an overflowing bin and track the repair.

options: A type of hospital bed only
A smaller area of a city
quiz.explain: Cities are divided into wards for better local government.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'ward' means only a hospital ward

quiz.q: Who represents the people of a ward in the municipal body?
quiz.explain: Each ward elects a councillor to speak for it in the municipal body.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up urban and rural representatives

quiz.q: How is a ward councillor chosen?
options: Elected by the voters of the ward
quiz.explain: The adult voters of the ward elect their councillor.

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of ward committees?
options: To deal with local problems closer to the people
To make laws for the whole country
quiz.explain: Ward committees help solve ward-level issues like drains, roads and cleanliness.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ward committees do national work

quiz.q: The 74th Amendment provides for ward committees in cities with a population of at least how many?
quiz.explain: Ward committees are to be set up in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more.

quiz.q: Which of these is a citizen's duty that helps the municipal body?
options: Segregating wet and dry waste at home
quiz.explain: Separating waste makes it easier to collect, compost and recycle.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how citizens help

quiz.q: A street in your ward is flooded every monsoon. Whom should residents first approach?
options: Their ward councillor or ward office
quiz.explain: Local problems are best taken first to the local ward office or councillor.
quiz.mistake: Takes a local problem to the highest authority first

quiz.q: Why is a city divided into wards?
options: So that each area's needs can be looked after better
To make the city smaller in size
quiz.explain: Smaller wards make it easier to know and solve local problems.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the purpose of dividing a city

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'My city is so huge! How does anyone know about the pothole on my street?'
teach.praise: Clever! The city is divided into wards, each with an elected councillor, and ward committees help solve local problems. I'll report the pothole!
